{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABYuM5uw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhCTPUc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 9, "title": "Complete remaining PC-9821 DOS game compatibility after partial Issue #7 implementation", "body": "## Problem

The closed [Issue #7](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/7) was **not functionally completed** by merged [PR #8](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/8). Its own description explicitly called the PR a *partial compatibility slice*. GitWeave's [post-merge comment](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/7#issuecomment-6306391145) confirms that closing #7 did not establish full acceptance. Track and implement the **remaining work** in this new Issue rather than treating the closed Issue as complete.

The repository already executes two independent, license-cleared PC-98 DOS applications (ADV98's playable Japanese sample and 98VIDEOP) with FreeDOS(98). It has selectable VM and experimental PC-9821Ap DOS profiles; 16-color four-plane graphics, Shinonome Japanese JIS glyphs, limited A20/extended RAM, approximate YM2203 OPN FM/SSG, save/reload and automated native + real-Wasm browser tests. **Preserve and extend that work; do not rewrite or duplicate it.** See [current compatibility matrix](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md).

**Product scope: 1990s PC-98/PC-9821 MS-DOS games, not Windows.** Do not add Windows 3.x/95/98 booting, Windows drivers, Win32/DirectX games or IBM VGA emulation.

**From-scratch rule:** CPU, memory, BIOS, graphics, disk, mouse, sound and other hardware emulation must remain original Rust code. Do not use, fork, translate, embed or port an existing x86/PC-98 emulator, chip emulator or emulation library. Non-emulation build tools, general UI/Wasm/testing tools, legally redistributable replacement fonts, and real third-party *guest* DOS software are allowed. No proprietary NEC firmware/font ROMs, unlicensed disk images or sound ROMs.

## Expected outcome

Complete the DOS-era PC-9821Ap compatibility gaps from #7 in the **existing Rust/Wasm emulator** and demonstrate the relevant hardware features by booting and interacting with independently authored, legally redistributable **real PC-98 DOS games and test utilities** through guest FreeDOS (not a host DOS interpreter or browser mock). Retain support for existing ADV98, 98VIDEOP, Star Trail, HelloWorld and the VM profile.

The objective is **broad PC-9821-era DOS game compatibility** rather than complete fidelity for every NEC machine or every game. Accurately document which machine, CPU, display, audio and BIOS capabilities are implemented and which remain untested. Use the actual [PC-9821Ap/U2 specification](https://support.nec-lavie.jp/support/product/data/spec/cpu/b211-1.html) and PC-98 I/O documentation, not IBM PC/AT assumptions.

### Remaining implementation work (do not redo the merged slice)

1. **386/486 DOS CPU semantics:** extend the original Rust CPU for 0x66/0x67 prefixes, EAX–EDI, 32-bit operand/address-size decoding and ModR/M/SIB, relevant 386/486 real-mode instructions, EFLAGS, correct segment/address arithmetic and fault/exception behavior. Ensure V30/VM-specific behavior is still selected by the existing machine profile. Test instruction edge cases and at least one independent DOS binary that actually executes added instructions. Support protected mode, DPMI or DOS extenders only where demonstrably required by accepted DOS titles; do not claim unimplemented 486/FPU behavior.
2. **Memory and firmware:** make the Ap profile's declared RAM genuinely usable with relevant PC-98 A20/HMA, expanded/extended memory access and XMS/EMS/INT 1F and BIOS interfaces as required by the selected DOS tests. Preserve correct ROM, VRAM and I/O holes, work areas, reset behavior and BIOS error returns. Avoid claiming a full physical 486/66 MHz timing model; improve scheduler timing only to the extent demanded by games and hardware tests.
3. **Bootable hard disk and media:** implement the PC-98 HDD controller interface(s) actually needed by chosen DOS titles (e.g. SASI/IDE; choose and document the real target rather than implementing all controllers speculatively), HDD IPL/BIOS services, validated disk-image geometry, sector reads/writes, mount/boot and save/export/reimport or persistence in native and browser builds. Include automated boot of a legally licensed PC-98 DOS installation from HDD and run a genuine DOS application on it. Maintain raw/D88 FDD tests and extend FDC formats/behavior where demanded by fixtures; reject malformed images safely.
4. **Graphics and character generation:** finish guest-visible GDC/GRCG/EGC operations required by actual games, including drawing/raster/scroll behavior and correct 16-color pages/palette; implement and test a real PC-9821 PEGC 256-color DOS graphics mode, relevant bank/window mapping and palette with a guest-driven independent 256-color fixture. Expand Japanese CG/ANK/kana/user-defined glyph behavior where required by selected titles using clearly redistributable data (keep Shinonome attribution; never copy NEC Kanji ROMs). Test guest VRAM/framebuffer pixels, rather than host-rendering a game's image.
5. **Mouse and input:** implement PC-98 mouse port/controller, cursor movement/button state, required IRQ/BIOS behavior and guest DOS driver interaction needed by an independent software fixture. Feed browser pointer events through emulated devices, not directly into application logic. Keep the existing keyboard and game controls.
6. **Sound-board compatibility:** expand original approximate YM2203/26K FM/SSG toward guest-used modes and add the PC-9801-86/YM2608 (OPNA) bank, FM/SSG, timers/IRQ, rhythm and ADPCM and/or 86 PCM paths required by real DOS game tests. Use properly licensed or independently synthesized sample data; no proprietary chip ROMs. **Enable game-driven music/sound**, not only the existing independent fm98.hdm tone harness: for ADV98, a license-cleared PMD-compatible driver/music path is one possible route, but a different legal DOS game with real music is acceptable. Capture guest-originated PCM in native tests and Web Audio in real-Wasm browser tests.
7. **Browser integration and compatibility regression:** expose appropriate profile/media controls for HDD, mouse, audio and display without sacrificing responsiveness. Continue to run the very same original Rust core natively and as Wasm; preserve static GitHub Pages deployment, local serving at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, and all existing demos. No backend emulator execution.

### Guest-first strategy and licensing

Use reproducible, machine-readable compatibility manifests recording original source/version/commit, hashes, feature requirements and **per-file** redistribution rights. Extend the existing pinned FreeDOS/ADV98/98VIDEOP fixtures with independent DOS programs that genuinely exercise the missing instructions and devices (especially a 256-color program, mouse use, HDD boot, and musical output). Source-level DOS utilities or small original targeted *device tests* may supplement verification, but are **not substitutes for actual third-party DOS game compatibility and game-originated audio**. A candidate may be downloaded or constructed for unattended tests **only** when its licensing permits this and its source/notice obligations are honored; user-supplied copyrighted games are optional, not required for CI or merge.

Prefer the smallest coherent real-hardware implementation proven by trace-driven compatibility tests. Do not hard-code guest/application names or screenshots into host or emulator behavior. A separate PR can implement a truthful, validated intermediate part, but it **must not close this Issue** or claim to satisfy the remaining milestone while acceptance gaps remain.

### Reference baseline

- [Issue #7 and its original acceptance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/7)
- [Merged partial PR #8](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/8)
- [Current DOS profile/known gaps](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md)
- [VM hardware map](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md)
- [Media and font licensing audit](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/licenses.md)
- [UNDOCUMENTED 9801/9821 I/O reference](https://www.webtech.co.jp/company/doc/undocumented_mem/index.html)
- [Repository development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)

## Context and reproduction

At the PR #8 baseline, [docs/dos-compatibility.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md) documents the following exact gaps: no 66/67 or 32-bit instruction/address decoding; extended RAM mostly inaccessible through guest CPU; no XMS/EMS or INT 1F copy; no HDD controller/boot; only half of Ap's graphics storage; no EGC, PEGC/256-color, 480-line display or GDC vector engine; incomplete Japanese ANK/CG; no mouse; incomplete YM2203 synthesis and no OPNA/rhythm/ADPCM/86 PCM; ADV98 plays silently without an optional music driver; and approximate fixed 8 MHz scheduler instead of full physical Ap timings. These are not completed merely by closing Issue #7.

Existing guest fixture setup and tests are documented in [README](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md) and [DOS compatibility instructions](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md). Inspect the actual latest `main` and preserve any subsequent improvements.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing PC-9801VM and Ap DOS profiles remain selectable and existing third-party ADV98/98VIDEOP, Star Trail, HelloWorld and FreeDOS fixtures pass unchanged or with justified updates. No Windows compatibility work is introduced.
- [ ] Original Rust 386/486 real-mode instruction/32-bit operand/address support is implemented and verified by native instruction/exception tests **and an independent guest DOS executable** using the new instructions. Architecture-specific VM regression coverage remains passing.
- [ ] The Ap extended-memory and BIOS behavior required by the accepted DOS programs is guest-accessible and tested; memory/address/ROM boundary and A20 behavior remain correct. Any unimplemented protected-mode/FPU/DPMI subset is clearly documented.
- [ ] A licensed PC-98 DOS guest **boots from an emulated HDD** under the Ap profile, loads and executes at least one independent DOS application, and demonstrates repeatable reads/writes and save/export/reimport or equivalent durable persistence; invalid/malicious images are rejected safely in native and browser tests.
- [ ] Guest-visible EGC/GDC behavior and a documented PC-9821 **256-color PEGC mode** are exercised by actual guest code, with reproducible palette/framebuffer assertions. Existing Japanese and 16-color ADV98 display regressions pass, and additional ANK/CG features exercised by guest fixtures are correctly rendered.
- [ ] A guest DOS application controls the **emulated PC-98 mouse** via its real port/BIOS/driver-visible interface. Automated browser pointer injection produces verifiable guest-owned mouse/button state and UI response.
- [ ] Game **music/sound comes from actual third-party DOS game execution** through emulated FM/OPNA/PCM hardware (as required by the selected game) into the browser audio pipeline. Native register/timer/IRQ/audio tests and actual-Wasm Web Audio checks verify non-silent guest-originated sound. The existing FM test alone does **not** meet this criterion.
- [ ] At least two independent third-party PC-98 DOS applications, including the playable ADV98 sample or another independently authored DOS game, still execute their own CPU instructions in the same emulator. New test fixtures exercise the extended CPU, HDD, mouse, 256-color video and musical output without host-side game behavior simulation; source hashes/license notices and reproducible build/download steps are recorded.
- [ ] No emulation library/copy/port or proprietary BIOS/ROM/OS/media is introduced. Only clearly redistributable fonts and media are included in GitHub Pages assets; DOS fixtures/guest sources remain properly licensed and packaged separately as needed.
- [ ] Before merge, run and pass the documented `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, real `wasm32-unknown-unknown` production build, fixture/provenance checks, and actual-Wasm Playwright/Chromium browser integration tests (at both local root and Pages subpath). Tests must verify guest execution, video, mouse, disk and game audio, not screenshots of a host-side mock. Report exact commands and results in the PR.
- [ ] Source-Issue review verifies both completeness and lack of unnecessary scope. **Do not close this Issue on a partial PR**, even if an upstream automation treats any merged PR as completion. If automation closes it prematurely, open a follow-up `task` Issue for remaining acceptance gaps instead of declaring success.

**No merge deadlock:** every pre-merge criterion must be achievable by automated checks on a PR branch. Do **not** require physical hardware, manual playtesting, subjective human approval, unavailable proprietary software, live Pages publication or checks only possible after merging. Use available license-cleared reproducible fixtures and AI review.

## Optional validation

More commercial games supplied by their lawful owners, physical PC-9821 comparisons, additional 486 protected-mode/DPMI/DOS-extender support, cycle/analog audio fidelity, wider SASI/IDE/SCSI/EGC/PEGC features and post-merge published-site verification. These do not block acceptance unless directly required by a selected automatic DOS-game test.

## Required post-merge verification

None as a prerequisite to issue completion or merge. A subsequent `main` push should trigger existing GitHub Pages Actions automatically; if live deployment or published runtime fails, register a **separate `task` Issue** with the run URL/error/reproduction. Never block this PR waiting for a deployment that only occurs after merge.
